lead: someone rang a friend of yours to ask whether you take that sort of work, and the friend said no on your behalf, warmly and with total confidence, and that has been the answer for six years.
sun: the work leaves bare and leaves good, and nothing travels beside it — no list of what can be done with it, no line about who gets one. a person who wants something has to guess, and guessing at a maker this good feels like bad manners, so they ask somebody who knows you instead. the asking has gone on for years, always somewhere else.
moon: where your terms would sit there is a blank, and a blank does not survive being looked at. it gets furnished by whoever was asked — in good faith, out of what a person who made that would surely require — and inside a year the furniture is quoted back to you as yours. nobody can point to the day it was decided, including you.
pull: there is a set of rules about your work, kept by people who love you, and not a line of it came from you. the invented guard does the job yours would have done.
tension: the rules are wrong in particular places. two of them have refused, on your behalf, exactly the work you would have gone anywhere for, and you learned about both afterwards, from somebody being funny about it. saying so now takes the standing off a friend who has spent six years defending a position he believed was yours — and the position has protected you, on other days, from people you would not have been able to turn down.
cost: work reaches you that never reaches people who publish their conditions — a stranger hires you on a friend's word, with nothing to negotiate and nothing to read first. what arrives has been sorted by somebody else's idea of you. the day one of them retires or falls out with you, the rules go with him, and the thing they were standing in front of has never been covered.

lead: he told you the true version in a car park, badly, at the end of a long night. what you made afterwards is accurate about that thing in a way nothing else is, and your name is on it.
sun: what you understand ends up in the work, because that is the one place anything of yours goes. and it goes in undisguised: no name changed, no case blurred, nothing moved a county over to make it unrecognisable, because the move that covers a thing on the way out has never been available to you. the finished piece is admired for exactly the part that could only have come from being told.
moon: people tell you things because you hear the sentence under the one they manage, and being heard that exactly is rare enough to keep them coming back. nothing gets repeated, ever. the hearing goes somewhere slower: into how you understand the thing itself, and the thing itself is what you make, in public, at the top of your ability.
pull: nobody has ever been quoted. one man reads the finished thing and finds a night of his own life in it, described better than he could, by somebody he chose to tell.
tension: there is no complaint available to him. no detail of his is in there, and he would have to describe what he told you in order to explain what he recognises, which is the one conversation he came to you to avoid having. so he says the warm thing about the work and goes quiet in a new way afterwards. the ones who tell you most are the ones who can see where it went.
cost: the unsayable version of a thing goes in front of people who were not there and lands, and the material for that only ever arrives in confidence. the piece goes out finished and signed, so the man who gave it to you meets it in a shop, in company, on an ordinary afternoon, and finds out then what his worst night was for.

lead: it comes through the wall, and it has been coming through the wall since before the couple next door had children. nobody on that landing has ever needed telling that it is good.
sun: the good passes and the wrong ones go out through the same wall at the same volume. nothing is kept back for a later hearing, no version gets worked up quietly before anybody is let near it, because working it quietly would be a covering and the covering move is missing. the neighbours have the whole history of every finished thing, including the parts you would not play for a friend.
moon: the way to find out whether a thing works is to put it out and read what comes back, so it goes out early and often, at whatever hour. a rhythm that regular gets built into other people's days: a baby settles to it, the man upstairs knows he is late by which passage he can hear, and a woman downstairs has never mentioned that she waits for it.
pull: every wrong pass you have made in twenty years was heard by somebody, and the same people run their evenings off the sound. the practice is as public as the piece.
tension: a wall gives away the hours and nothing else, so the account of you held in that building is a schedule with a talent attached. they are proud of it. what nobody out there can hear is which pass was the one that worked — an evening of failure and the evening it came right sound alike through brick, so the best night of your working life was somebody else's ordinary tuesday, and they were pleased you were in.
cost: a hundred wrong passes at full volume is a method, and it is why the right one arrives sooner here than for people who work behind a door. the method has no quiet setting. nothing you have attempted is unheard, nobody near you has met a finished thing of yours fresh, and the fondness in that building and the timekeeping came in as a single arrangement.

lead: the back room has had four people in it in eleven years, and you asked each of them yourself, on an evening you could name. the choosing has never once turned on what a person would do in there.
sun: the house is where the work lives, unlocked and unlisted, because putting things away has never been something that happens here. finished pieces, the ones that failed, the letters about all of it — a guest lives among them for months. whoever has the back room has closer access to the whole of it than any buyer, any friend, anybody who has ever written about it.
moon: the room is given, deliberately, to whoever is in the worst position that year — a decision you make in a week, alone, and can account for. need is the whole of the test. what a person in trouble does with unattended things has never formed itself into a question in time to be asked, and asking it would end the practice it was meant to protect.
pull: you decide who stands nearest the one thing in your life that nobody is minding, and the decision is made entirely on who is having the worst year.
tension: three of the four went well and the fourth is the story that gets told about you now, fondly, as a warning, with the word soft in it. he was genuinely in trouble — that part was read correctly. what he left with had been lying in the open for months, and the only kind of room that would have caught him is one with a gate on it, which is a different house and a different offer.
cost: a person at the end of their rope can be delivered to your door at any hour and get a real room, not a sofa — a decision made in advance. the same door is the only one your work is behind, so the years you were most useful to somebody in trouble are the years the whole of it was standing open, and the two do not run separately.
